title: Outer event radii grew without a clear median radius change in three USGS first-month earthquake samples
abstract: We compared cumulative outer radii with median radii in fixed USGS catalogs for Ridgecrest, Stanley, and Monte Cristo. The main samples use preferred magnitude at least 2.5 on days 1 to 30 in 100 km query regions. Outer-radius slopes were 10.56, 22.13, and 46.30 km per log-time decade. Shuffling distances among fixed event times gave upper-tail fractions of 0.913, 0.011, and 0.010. Median radius changes from days 1 to 8 to days 15 to 30 were 0.90, 1.21, and -0.16 km. All daily resampling ranges included zero. At Stanley the outer-radius result weakened at other magnitude floors. At Monte Cristo it weakened at magnitude 3 when the first day was omitted. Record growth and change in a typical event radius thus give different evidence. These conditional catalog checks do not prove stable radii, physical migration, or fluid flow. We extend prior campaign spatial audits with a count-preserving record test and a third sequence. The package includes event data, source hashes, code, figures, and an offline repeat path.

display.caption: Cumulative maximum radii and daily radius summaries at preferred magnitude at least 2.5. Gray ranges are pointwise shuffle ranges, not simultaneous confidence bands.

citations.reason: Extends the published Monte Cristo boundary audit with cumulative radius records and a fixed-time shuffle.
Extends the Ridgecrest spatial audit with a record statistic, a different window comparison, and two more sequences.
